extracted.intended_audience: authors, journal editors, and peer reviewers of qualitative research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Standards (SRQR) for transparent reporting of qualitative research, consisting of a 21-item checklist covering title/abstract through funding/conflicts; intended to guide authors in writing and reviewers in appraising qualitative manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise description of the nature and topic of the study, identifying whether it's qualitative and indicating the approach or data collection methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should clearly state that the study is qualitative and name the qualitative approach or data collection methods in the title/abstract to improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the problem being studied (problem formulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose or research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear statement of the purpose of the study or the research question(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative approach and research paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the qualitative approach and research paradigm (e.g., ethnography, grounded theory, case study, phenomenology, narrative research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the specific methodological approach and the underlying paradigm to situate methods and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher characteristics and reflexivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of researcher characteristics and reflexivity (how researcher background, perspectives, and interactions may influence the research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should particularly attend to researcher reflexivity when assessing qualitative manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the context in which the research was conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the sampling strategy used to select participants or data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of ethical issues and approvals relevant to the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description of the data collection methods used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection instruments and technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the instruments and technologies used to collect data (e.g., interview guides, recording devices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of study
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of the units of study (e.g., participants, documents, observations) and their characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of data processing procedures (e.g., transcription, data management, coding preparations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the data analysis methods and procedures used to generate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques to enhance trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques used to enhance the trustworthiness of the analysis (e.g., triangulation, member checking, audit trails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should attend to how authors demonstrate trustworthiness of their analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesis and interpretation of findings—how data were integrated to produce interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to empirical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to empirical data (e.g., illustrative quotes, excerpts) that support analytic findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six SRQR topical sections; encompasses title/abstract and introduction elements such as problem formulation and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Introduction' section to report problem formulation and research questions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: Method
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six SRQR topical sections covering methodological reporting (approach, researcher reflexivity, context, sampling, ethics, data collection, instruments, units, processing, analysis, trustworthiness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Method section transparently reports approach, researcher characteristics, context, sampling, ethical oversight, and data procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six SRQR topical sections where findings/synthesis and links to empirical data are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present synthesized findings alongside empirical data that illustrate and support interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the six SRQR topical sections for interpreting results, implications, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (conflict of interest, funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other reporting items including conflict of interest and funding disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and any conflicts of interest as part of transparent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use / checklist application
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for peer reviewers to check that all 21 SRQR items are reported in qualitative manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing qualitative research, peer reviewers should check that all 21 SRQR items are reported, particularly attending to researcher reflexivity and the trustworthiness of analysis.
